title: Aspiration event
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Stop the feed and escalate when respiratory distress follows a feed.
Do not use a tube again until its position is confirmed by the approved method.
Know that listening over the stomach is not a safe check.

sources.use: NICE CG32 nasogastric tube position confirmation statements
NHS misplaced nasogastric tube patient safety alert

required_sources: Aspiration management guideline (airway clearing, suction, radiology) read in full
Unit enteral feeding and tube-position policy
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.
First-line airway management after aspiration is not drawn from a source read and is not written.
The approved position check differs by country and product; the scenario names no pH threshold.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
setting: A fictional adult receiving enteral feed through a nasogastric tube on a fictional unit.

steps.info: Soon after a feed starts the patient coughs, becomes breathless and the saturation falls.

options.text: Stop the feed, call for help, assess airway and breathing and keep the head of the bed raised.
options.feedback: The NHS alert on misplaced tubes calls for stopping feed or medicines through a tube whose position is in doubt, and head-of-bed elevation is an essential practice; calling for help is part of the response.
options.consequence: Help arrives while the feed is stopped and the patient is supported.

options.text: Slow the feed and watch for a while.
options.feedback: Continuing the feed after respiratory distress risks more harm.
options.consequence: The patient's breathing worsens as feed continues.

options.text: Flush the tube to clear it and carry on.
options.feedback: Introducing fluid into a tube of uncertain position risks harm.

steps.info: The team is at the bedside and asks whether the tube can be used.

options.text: Do not use the tube for feed or medicines until its position has been confirmed by the approved method under the unit's policy and the team agrees.
options.feedback: NICE and the NHS alert say position must be confirmed by an approved method before use, and unreliable methods must not be used.
options.consequence: The tube position is checked properly and the plan is agreed.

options.text: Restart the feed because the position was checked yesterday.
options.feedback: Position is confirmed before each use according to the policy, not carried over from an earlier check.
options.consequence: The feed restarts through a tube that may be misplaced.

options.text: Confirm the position by listening over the stomach while air is injected.
options.feedback: NICE lists listening over the stomach as an unsafe method.
options.consequence: A misplaced tube is wrongly accepted.

steps.info: The patient is stable and the charge nurse asks for a report.

options.text: Give a factual SBAR, record the event and report it through the incident system, noting the position checks done and the feed timing.
options.feedback: Misplaced-tube feeding is a patient-safety event that is reported so the contributing factors can be reviewed.
options.consequence: The review includes how the position was checked.

options.text: Record only that the patient coughed.
options.feedback: An incomplete record loses the timing and the checks.
options.consequence: The review cannot reconstruct what happened.

options.text: Say nothing, as the patient recovered.
options.feedback: Events are reported so that they can be learned from.

learning_points: Stop the feed and call for help when distress follows a feed.
Confirm tube position by the approved method before use and never by listening over the stomach.
